question.text: Kavita, a salaried individual, has a total income of Rs.7,15,000 under the new tax regime for FY 2024-25. Her computed tax liability before rebate is Rs.28,000. What is her final tax liability after applying Section 87A rebate and marginal relief?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the new regime for FY 2024-25, Section 87A rebate is available only if total income does not exceed Rs.7,00,000. Kavita's income of Rs.7,15,000 exceeds that threshold, so she is not eligible for the rebate. Marginal relief then applies: tax payable is limited to the amount by which income exceeds Rs.7,00,000. The excess is Rs.7,15,000 - Rs.7,00,000 = Rs.15,000, which is lower than the computed tax of Rs.28,000, so the final tax is capped at Rs.15,000. The Trap: Option A (Rs.28,000) ignores marginal relief. Option B (Rs.0) wrongly assumes the 87A rebate still applies above Rs.7,00,000. Option D (Rs.3,000) incorrectly computes the result as tax minus rebate (Rs.28,000 - Rs.25,000) instead of capping tax at the excess income. Note: Explanation sentence repaired and rewritten cleanly around the marginal-relief cap; unsupported framing removed.
